semanticDeltaReview.detail: Taller 100 by 84 bounds and uniform fitting preserve incidence, angles and distance ratios; circles are included in fit extents. No renderer or gate changes. All labels remain associated with the intended construction.

The arbitrary internal tangency point X is at polar angle 90 degrees instead of 105; the alternate 75-degree construction is retained. Tangency, equality of tangent segments and angle-bisector coordinate assertions pass. Both displayed configurations satisfy the unchanged condition.

Acute and obtuse isosceles alternatives are fitted separately and never coexist in one view. With base 8, heights 12 and 2.8 respectively keep the apex acute and obtuse; each construction retains circumcentre and incentre, both circles and the axis. The obtuse circumcentre remains outside the triangle.

X remains at its original coordinate (0,1), distinct from O in the main construction. Moving unlabelled axis support points from ±4 to ±3 does not change that line. The X=O counterexample is still shown, and its two valid angle-bisector axes remain. O=X is now labelled O with an explicit X=O note. The independent caption finding was corrected to A₁B₁.

Changed arbitrary D and S example coordinates still define the same reflection construction and satisfy all original assertions. Special parallel, perpendicular and coincident-line alternatives are preserved.

A separate label-only LA anchor carries a=a₁ without adding a geometric point. The diameter case retains a=a₁ perpendicular to b, both intersections yielding the same unoriented segment. Its shared centre/midpoint is labelled O and the note explicitly states O=H. All five alternatives are retained.

The ordinary two-bisector-axis case and perpendicular four-axis case are both shown. The single point O is distinguishable from the line labels and angle marks; no axes or mathematical alternatives were removed.
